_: The King's one objective at a time (reign.js LADDER; Warcraft III's and Age of Empires II's campaign objectives; Mac 2026-11-15: 'I literally don't know what to do... just make the game fun'). The war king from minute one: beat the raiders, raise the levy, march on a town, win a house's oath; past these, the realm's own (reign.js nextAim). Each step: key, do (the verb, for the next line), text (the line top-left; {town} is the raided town, {seat} the King's seat, {prize} and {house} the nearest town a great house holds and its house; with none, 'a town'), wait (the line before its moment has come, as the raiders before they cross), how (its tooltip), input (the exact hand on mouse and keys, shown beside the line for the first steps only), met (the rule: raiders, companies, town, oath), its numbers (n companies, to favour), reward (gold, knights, feast) and says (the chronicle's line and the tick when done). A step already true when the reign begins is passed over, but never raiders or town.

raiders._near: tiles from a royal town within which a wild house's soldiers count as raiding it

steps.text: Raiders burn {town}. Select your host and right-click them.
steps.wait: Raiders are seen on the border. Make ready your host.
steps.how: Click your host's banner to select it, then right-click the raiders: your men march and fight them.
steps.says: The raiders are broken and flee. The townsfolk send the King a purse of thanks.

steps.how: Open {seat}'s card and raise the levy, or call the banners.
steps.says: Two thousand four hundred men stand under the royal banner. Two knights ride in to join them, unasked.

steps.how: Select your host, right-click {prize} and besiege it until it yields. Click this line to see it.
steps.says: A new town flies the royal banner. Its people line the road to see the King's men ride in.

steps.text: Win a great house's oath to the Crown.
steps.how: Favour a house until it stands at 70: a gift, a feast, a match, or a ruling in its favour.
steps.says: A great house swears itself to the Crown, and sends a chest of silver to prove it.
